correctness.rationale: The complete proof correctly applies the primary article’s equality X=U∪P0∪P1 and odd-n contractibility of U, both of which were checked at the actual original lemmas. Signed fixed-orbit Lefschetz traces of cycle independence complexes give the full rotations and reflections, with correct augmented empty-face sign and degree d=floor((n+1)/3). Reflection quotient is path P_{(n-1)/2}; rotation quotient has g=gcd(n,j) orbit classes, including the looped g=1 convention. The resulting H character and coset-induction formula cover every element of D_{2n}; the n=3,5,7,9,11 cases and boundary congruences match independent exact direct simplicial traces.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original contribution is the natural G-equivariant relative-chain identification for odd Möbius-ladder perfect-matching complexes and the resulting full induced rational G-module. The full cycle matching-complex D_n character, which exactly supplies the cycle W_n building block, is already in a separate published result; its characters and six-periodic recurrence are not claimed new. Agarwal–Basak proved nonequivariant decomposition and sphere counts but not the natural full G-action. The previously published half-turn calculation is one strict restriction of the present character. The combination via a G-equivariant relative pair is short and uses standard homological algebra, but requires establishing component stability and transitive coset permutation; no inspected prior statement explicitly supplies that induction for this graph family. Originality is limited to that structural lift and its exact-object application; precedence risk is retained.
residual_risks: The theorem is a concise combination of prior exact decomposition, published cycle characters, and standard naturality; a different novelty standard might regard this as a routine immediate corollary. We regard the new explicit G-module lift for this natural graph family as a motivated structural fact.
Equivalent unindexed independent full dihedral ladder character calculations may exist.
An all-parameter formal equivariant chain certification is not provided; new direct finite checks cover only n=3,5,7,9,11.
